gap: No result ChatGPT got says which small stations take a router's 12 V barrel plug directly. Tenergy's own spec page lists two 12 V 8 A DC sockets of size 5521 (5.5×2.1 mm) on the T320, but says nothing about a UPS or pass-through function. BLUETTI's US page gives the Elite 30 V2 a ≤10 ms UPS with 980 W bypass but does not list its barrel-port rating.
standout_why: I compared against the four cited pages: homepowerfacts.com, outagemath.com, backupcalc.com and our own Dealectric page. I also checked the top results of today's run of the same query, which are mostly Anker SOLIX and other maker blogs. homepowerfacts marks every station 'Yes' and says to use a DC output 'where your device allows it' without naming any model that has one. backupcalc says to use 'a barrel-plug adapter from the car socket' and gives no plug size or model. outagemath lists router adapter voltages (eero 5 V, Nest Wifi Pro 10 V, Archer AX21 12 V 1.5 A, R7000 12 V 3.5 A) but no station ports, barrel sizes or switchover times. None of them pairs a specific station's 5.5×2.1 mm 12 V socket with a router, and none notes that Tenergy publishes no UPS for the T320.
decides: This confirms the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 as the pick for a router that must not drop during an outage. BLUETTI states a ≤10 ms switchover and 980 W bypass, and the price is $289.99. The Tenergy T320 ($225.99) is the cheaper way to run a 12 V router or modem without the inverter, through a plain 5.5×2.1 mm cable from its 12 V 8 A sockets. But Tenergy's page states no UPS or pass-through function, so you would plug the router in when the power fails. RIVER 3 and Explorer 240 v2 need a car-socket-to-barrel adapter, per our current page. Routers that take 5 V USB-C or 10 V (eero, Nest Wifi Pro, per outagemath's adapter list) can't use any of these 12 V barrel sockets directly.

findings.label: 12 V barrel (DC5521) outputs
findings.value: 2 sockets, 12 V 8 A each, socket size 5521 (5.5×2.1 mm)
findings.source_title: Tenergy T320 Portable Power Station 300Wh Backup Lithium Battery (Tenergy Power store)
findings.note: Quoted from the Technical Specifications: 'DC socket 1: 12V, 8A (socket size: 5521)' and 'DC socket 2: 12V, 8A (socket size: 5521)'. A router or modem with a 12 V 5.5×2.1 mm input, such as the 12 V 1.5 A Archer AX21 and 12 V 3.5 A R7000 adapters outagemath lists, falls within the rating, but check the plug size on your own adapter.

findings.label: DC and USB output limits, car port
findings.value: 120 W max continuous DC; car port 12 V 10 A; USB-C PD 45 W (5/9/12/15 V 3 A, 20 V 2.25 A); 69 W max continuous USB
findings.source_title: Tenergy T320 Portable Power Station 300Wh Backup Lithium Battery (Tenergy Power store)
findings.note: Taken from the maker's spec table. A 10–20 W router plus modem is far below the 120 W DC limit.

findings.label: UPS / pass-through function

findings.note: I read the whole product page for a UPS, switchover or pass-through statement and found none. Treat the T320 as a station you connect by hand after the power fails, not a seamless UPS.

findings.value: Battery fell about 10% over 4 h 'with DC power on'; ports must be switched on before they deliver power
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 30 V2 Review (MacRumors, Juli Clover, 2025-12-04)
findings.note: 10% of 288 Wh ≈ 28.8 Wh over 4 h, about 7 W. The review doesn't say whether anything was plugged in, so don't use this as an idle-draw figure. Clover also says she did not test the 10 ms switchover herself.
